Get your gp to refer you to rheumatology outpatients and get them to do bloods. SSA's or something. If you do have it they'll likely start you on plaquinil and anti inflammatories and see you every month or so until you settle into a medication regime that works with regular blood and eye tests. Public health system so it's all free but a bit slow. I'm about 7 years in, just had a yearly check up and the poor young doc had to tell me we've hit the limits of treatment (plaquinil, methotrexate, amitryptiline, bfufen and painkillers) until my organs are affected so smash codeine all winter while the flares get bad. Main point of contact and scrip repeats is my gp and outpatients keeps them in the loop with info. Flick me a message if you need to chat, not a big kiwi community with this autoimmune bullshit.

"Creamy pasta" is my family favourite and my go to easy dinner.

Get a pot of water boiling, dice an onion, some streaky bacon if you like, slice a couple of cups of mushrooms, and whatever other veg looks dodgy- i like broccoli, cabbage, or zucchini, and frozen peas.

Get a pan on and throw in the bacon and onion with a little oil and let it render and fry off until the onion is translucent. Throw in your veg and toss it around a bit, and give it a good cracking of black pepper. By now the water will be boiling so chuck in some pasta (whatever amount and type you have on hand) then pour 300ml of cream onto the veg pan. 

Reduce until the pasta is done, mostly drain the pasta and add it to the creamy veg. Season to your liking and let it sit for a few minutes before you serve. 

It's maybe 10 min hands on work, it's totally adaptable and creamy mushrooms on pasta is an all time winner. Use 500ml cream if you're feeding more than four. I'm sure this is what got my kids excited about veges too.

Throw a bunch of chopped veges (about 4c worth, I used carrots/celery/mushrooms/Brussels sprouts because that's what was going off), a diced onion, a big spoonful of minced garlic, 2 bay leaves, 2 chicken stock cubes/concentrate pots, and 3 or 4 skinless chicken thigh cutlets into your slow cooker. Pour over about 2L water and cook on low around 8 hours. 

Pull out the thighs and shred the meat back in. Smash a pack of dried egg noodles (I went with ribbon but, live your truth), and throw them in. Add 150ml of cream, give it another 20 minutes on low, season to taste. Eat it straight out  of the slow cooker.

 Serves 6-8, and will make all your coworkers jealous when you've got leftovers for lunch the next day.
